{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: CLI release smoke

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  schedule:
    - cron: "30 4 * * 1"

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: "${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}"
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  release-smoke:
    timeout-minutes: 20
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    environment:
      name: development
    env:
      DATABASE_URL: postgres://
      AUTH_SECRET: test
      WEBSTUDIO_RELEASE_SMOKE_TOKEN_BUDGET: 6000
      WEBSTUDIO_RELEASE_SMOKE_REPORT: ${{ github.workspace }}/artifacts/cli-release-smoke.json
      WEBSTUDIO_RELEASE_SMOKE_AGENT_COMMAND: ${{ vars.CLI_RELEASE_SMOKE_AGENT_COMMAND }}
      WEBSTUDIO_RELEASE_SMOKE_AGENT_REPORT: ${{ github.workspace }}/artifacts/cli-release-smoke-model.json
      CLI_RELEASE_SMOKE_AGENT_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.CLI_RELEASE_SMOKE_AGENT_API_KEY }}

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: ./.github/actions/submodules-checkout
        with:
          submodules-ssh-key: ${{ secrets.PRIVATE_GITHUB_DEPLOY_TOKEN }}

      - uses: ./.github/actions/ci-setup

      - name: Run packaged CLI and agent onboarding smoke
        run: pnpm --filter webstudio test:release-smoke

      - name: Upload compact comparison report
        if: ${{ always() }}
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: cli-release-smoke-comparison
          path: artifacts/cli-release-smoke.json
          if-no-files-found: error

      - name: Upload dual-package model evaluation report
        if: ${{ always() && vars.CLI_RELEASE_SMOKE_AGENT_COMMAND != '' }}
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: cli-release-smoke-model-evaluation
          path: artifacts/cli-release-smoke-model.json
          if-no-files-found: error",
  "rationale": "Applied P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE (cancel superseded/stale runs). The workflow is triggered by both schedule and workflow_dispatch on the same branch, so overlapping runs can consume runner time for the same smoke-test check. Adding a top-level concurrency group keyed by workflow and ref with cancel-in-progress cancels the older in-progress run when a newer revision starts, while the newest run always completes to preserve build/test coverage. The change is minimal: it adds no new permissions, secrets, network access, or deployment/publishing steps, and leaves all existing jobs, steps, timeouts, environment settings, and required checks intact. Preconditions are met (same workflow+branch grouping; newer run supersedes older). The release/deployment contraindication was assessed as not applying because this is a verification smoke test on a development environment rather than an actual deployment, and cancel-in-progress leaves the latest run to finish.",
  "evidence_ids": ["experiment:batch-scenario-three-run-560f8aa17cf2dbe5"]
}
